extracted_data.document_summary: This study aimed to develop and validate computationally efficient Polygenic Risk Score (PRS) models, including penalized logistic regression (lasso, elastic net, stepwise) and a Bayesian framework (S4), for predicting epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) risk. The main finding was that the S4 model, utilizing 27,240 SNPs, demonstrated the strongest association with non-mucinous EOC risk across diverse ancestral populations (European, East Asian, African) and in BRCA1/2 pathogenic variant carriers, offering improved risk prediction capabilities compared to existing approaches.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Polygenic Risk Score (PRS) modeling and risk prediction methodologies for Epithelial Ovarian Cancer (EOC) risk.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study compared multiple PRS models, including penalized logistic regression (lasso, elastic net, stepwise) and a Bayesian framework (S4), LDPred, and Select and Shrink models. These models were optimized using varying parameters such as tuning parameters (e.g., "λ" from 3.0 to 5.5, "κ" from -3.0 to 1) and shrinkage parameters (a, b, "φ" for S4). The S4 model, incorporating 27,240 SNPs, was identified as the most effective. Model performance was evaluated using metrics like AUC, Odds Ratio, and Hazard Ratio across different populations and genetic backgrounds. There were no direct dose-response comparisons for a therapeutic agent, as the study's scope was methodological and predictive.

analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Genotype data from blood samples of 23,564 non-mucinous EOC cases and 40,138 controls (model development), and validated in 198,101 women of European ancestries, 7,669 women of East Asian ancestries, 1,072 women of African ancestries, 18,915 BRCA1 pathogenic variant carriers, and 12,337 BRCA2 pathogenic variant carriers.
analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Genetic risk assessment (Polygenic Risk Score calculation) based on Single Nucleotide Polymorphism (SNP) genotype data

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: For the S4 model (27,240 SNPs), the odds ratios (OR) per unit standard deviation for non-mucinous EOC risk were: 1.38 (95% CI: 1.28–1.48, AUC: 0.588) in women of European ancestries; 1.14 (95% CI: 1.08–1.19, AUC: 0.538) in women of East Asian ancestries; and 1.38 (95% CI: 1.21–1.58, AUC: 0.593) in women of African ancestries. Hazard ratios were: 1.36 (95% CI: 1.29–1.43, AUC: 0.592) in BRCA1 pathogenic variant carriers; and 1.49 (95% CI: 1.35–1.64, AUC: 0.624) in BRCA2 pathogenic variant carriers. The S4 model showed the strongest association among tested models.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Quantifies an individual's cumulative genetic predisposition to complex diseases, reflecting the combined effect of multiple common genetic variants (SNPs) on disease susceptibility.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Risk prediction for invasive non-mucinous Epithelial Ovarian Cancer (EOC) using advanced Polygenic Risk Score (PRS) models, specifically the S4 Bayesian framework, in different ancestral populations and BRCA1/2 pathogenic variant carriers.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates an individual's genetic susceptibility to non-mucinous EOC, providing a tool for improved risk stratification and potential targeting for prevention programs. Higher PRS is associated with an increased risk of EOC.
analyzed_biomarkers.research_outlook: Incorporation of the S4 PRS in risk prediction models for ovarian cancer may have clinical utility in ovarian cancer prevention programs. Further optimization of PRS models for diverse populations and specific clinical scenarios should be explored.

analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Genetic data (from individuals of European ancestries)
analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Risk prediction model performance (AUC, Odds Ratio, Cumulative Risk)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: The S4 PRS model had an AUC = 0.593, and the elastic net model had an AUC = 0.586. Women in the top 95th percentile of the lasso derived PRS model had a 2.23-fold increased odds of non-mucinous EOC (95% CI: 1.64 - 3.02) compared to the middle quintile. Estimated cumulative risk of EOC by age 80 for women at the 99th centile of the S4 PRS was 2.81% versus 0.56% at the 1st centile.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Genetic risk assessment for complex diseases, aggregating effects of multiple genetic variants.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Prediction of non-mucinous Epithelial Ovarian Cancer (EOC) risk in women of European ancestries using various PRS models.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates personalized lifetime risk of EOC, allowing for stratification of individuals into different risk categories.
analyzed_biomarkers.research_outlook: Further refinement of PRS models to enhance predictive accuracy and clinical utility in European populations, potentially integrating with other risk factors.

analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Genetic data (from BRCA1 and BRCA2 pathogenic variant carriers)
analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Risk prediction model performance (Hazard Ratio, Absolute Risk)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: The S4 PRS model consistently showed the strongest association and predictive accuracy for invasive EOC risk. For BRCA1 carriers, the estimated absolute risk of EOC by age 80 at the 99th PRS centile was 68.4% (S4 model) versus 24.2% at the 1st centile. For BRCA2 carriers, it was 36.9% (S4 model) versus 6.92% at the 1st centile.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Modulation of hereditary cancer risk by accounting for the polygenic background in individuals with known high-risk genetic mutations.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Prediction of invasive EOC risk in BRCA1/BRCA2 pathogenic variant carriers.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Refines individual risk assessment in high-risk populations, potentially guiding more personalized surveillance or prophylactic strategies beyond known monogenic risk.
analyzed_biomarkers.research_outlook: Investigate the integration of PRS into clinical guidelines for BRCA1/BRCA2 carriers to personalize risk management and improve patient outcomes.

analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Genetic data (from individuals of East Asian ancestries)
analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Risk prediction model performance (AUC, Odds Ratio)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: The elastic net PRS was the best discriminative model with an AUC = 0.543. Women in the top 5% of the elastic net PRS had about a 1.60-fold increased risk of non-mucinous EOC (95% CI: 1.28–2.01) compared to the middle quintile. The odds ratio per unit standard deviation for the lasso model was 1.16 (95% CI: 1.11–1.22).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Genetic risk assessment for complex diseases, with observed differences in effect sizes across ancestral groups due to variant frequency variations.

analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Genetic Risk Prediction / Predictive Model Performance

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Most PRS models had higher effect estimates compared to previous approaches. AUC estimates for adjusted PLR methods were higher than PRS HGS for BRCA1 carriers (0.604). For BRCA2 carriers, lasso and S4 models showed slightly better AUC (0.667) than PRS HGS, while elastic net was comparable. AUC estimates for the general population in UK Biobank were slightly higher than estimates from previously published PRS models by Jia et al. (AUC = 0.57) and Yang et al. (AUC = 0.58). The risk for women above the 95th percentile of the PRS was similar to that conferred by pathogenic variants in moderate penetrance genes such as FANCM (RR = 2.1, 95% CI = 1.1–3.9) and PALB2 (RR = 2.91, 95% CI = 1.40–6.04).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Quantifies an individual's cumulative genetic predisposition to Epithelial Ovarian Cancer by integrating effects of multiple genetic variants (SNPs).

analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Provides sufficient discrimination for EOC risk, particularly in women of European ancestries, making it suitable for future consideration in risk prediction and prevention strategies for EOC.
analyzed_biomarkers.research_outlook: Further studies are required to optimize PRSs in ancestrally diverse populations and to validate their performance with the inclusion of other genetic and lifestyle risk factors.
